newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgarian lev ends down vs dlr despite c bank help.
newsitem.headline: Bulgarian lev ends down vs dlr despite c bank help.

text.p: The lev fell to 283-285 per dollar at the close of the interbank market from 277-280 in the morning as foreign currency demand heavily topped supply and despite dollar sales by the central bank, dealers said.
"A strong dollar-bullish sentiment persisted throughout the day while supply from commercial banks was very low," a bank dealer said.

Interbank trade was rather also nervous as growing pressure on the lev was carried over from the cash market amid Bulgarians' concerns about the safety of their lev savings under a currency board system being discussed for Bulgaria.
"If it was not for central bank sales, the dollar could have risen by some 10-15 levs today," another dealer said.
The central bank sold light foreign currency volumes at 276-278 levs per dollar on the interbank market, slowing down the fall, traders said.
Central bank officials were not available for comment.

People queued outside branches of the State Savings Bank (SSB) to withdraw lev deposits and stashed them at home or converted them into hard currency out of fear they might lose their savings under a currency board system, traders said.
More than four billion levs were withdrawn from the SSB by panic-stricken Bulgarians since early last week, but queues were starting to die down, SSB head Bistra Dimitrova told Reuters on Tuesday.
An International Monetary Fund (IMF) mission, which left last week, proposed setting up of a currency board to stabilise the lev, defeat hyperinflation and boost economic growth.

Under the scheme, the lev is to be pegged to a major currency and the amount of levs in circulation must be exactly matched by the central bank's foreign currency reserves. -- Anastas Petrov, Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-876032
